title: Ah, taci, ingiusto core!
subtitle: Donna Elvira, Don Giovanni and Leporello: trio from Don Giovanni, Act 2 (No. 15)

passages.label: Ah, taci, ingiusto core! · Zitto! di Donna Elvira
Cogliere io vo' il momento · Elvira, idolo mio! · Sì, vita mia, son io
Numi, che strano effetto · State a veder la pazza · Discendi, o gioja bella
No, non ti credo · Ah, credemi! · Se seguitate, io rido
Dei, che cimento è questo! · Spero che cada presto · Già quel mendace labbro
Dei, che cimento (again) · Più fertile talento (to the end)

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527 (1787), Act 2 scene 2, No. 15 Trio
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Lorenzo Da Ponte, libretto of Don Giovanni (1787)
licences.author: Lorenzo Da Ponte (1749–1838)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score (gioja, quà, sò, son' io; "strano effetto" where the libretto has "strano affetto"; Giovanni's "credemi" for the libretto's "credimi"; Leporello's "State a veder la pazza" where the libretto has "State a veder che la pazza"; "oh Dei" for "o Dei").

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 164–171, bars 1–84 of No. 15
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics, slurs and other marks, then checked bar by bar and checked again by a fresh checker (clean). The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Two print slips are read by the bar's sum: in bar 49 the piano's first chord (D4+A4), printed with an eighth flag, is a sixteenth, and in bar 62 Elvira's E4 after the dotted G#4, printed with one flag, is a sixteenth. Playback tempo: ♩ = 51 (a dotted quarter = 34), about 4:56, from the median (4:59) of five complete recordings (Solti 1996 4:38, Giulini 1959 4:49, Fricsay 1958 4:59, Karajan 1985 5:03, Böhm 1977 5:18); Mozart gives the word Andantino only.
